title: When the honeymoon ends
hook: If Islam feels less exciting than it did in week one, nothing is wrong with you. You're right on schedule.

screens.text: The first weeks can feel bright: everything new, every prayer a big moment. Then one day it's just… Tuesday. Today is about that day, because almost every convert meets it.
**It has a name: the honeymoon ending.** Around a month in, many converts notice the glow fade. It's one of the most common things converts describe. It's a stage, not a verdict [Field Guide ch. 18].
bubbles: Fajr gets hard. Prayer feels like a routine. The people who hugged you at your shahada got busy.
A quiet voice asks, "Did I make the right decision?" That question shows up for many converts around now.

screens.text: Faith has ups and downs. Look at the whole line, not one low point.

points.label: Week 1
points.text: Everything is new. Every prayer feels like a big moment.

points.label: About a month in
points.text: The glow fades. Prayer feels like routine, and people got busy.

points.label: A low day
points.text: You pray anyway, with what you have, and tell someone you're struggling.

points.label: Over time
points.text: Small, steady steps and good company carry you through the dips.

screens.title: What the slump is, and what it isn't

cards.front: "If I feel low, I must be losing my faith."
cards.back: Feeling low is not leaving Islam. Leaving is a choice to reject it. A tired heart that keeps praying is a believing heart.
They do. One of the Prophet's ﷺ own Companions felt it so strongly he called himself a hypocrite. (More on the next screen.)

cards.front: "My prayer doesn't count if I feel nothing."
cards.back: It counts. Feelings come and go; the prayer you showed up for is still yours. Showing up on a flat day may even mean more.

cards.front: "I should take a break until I feel it again."
cards.back: All five prayers stay due, so pray them with what you have. Small and steady beats big and burned out.
Asking hard questions is human. What matters is that you bring them to Allah and to people who can help, not that you never have them.

screens.text: **Remember Hanzalah from Day 12?** His faith felt strong beside the Prophet ﷺ and faded at home, and he feared he was a hypocrite. The answer he got still holds: there is a time for this and a time for that [Muslim 2750].
bubbles: A slump after the first weeks is that same pattern, not a sign you chose wrong.

screens.situation: Marcus hasn't felt anything in prayer for a week. He missed Asr yesterday and feels like a fake. What's his best next step?

options.text: Pray the next prayer anyway, make up Asr, and text a Muslim friend that he's in a slump
options.feedback: Yes. Keep the basics, repair what was missed, and don't carry it alone. That's how slumps pass.

options.text: Wait until the feeling comes back, then start praying again
options.feedback: Not quite. The feeling often comes back *through* praying, not before it. Keep the five.

options.text: Add hours of extra prayer and fasting to fix it fast
options.feedback: Kind instinct, but that often leads to burnout. Small, regular deeds are what Allah loves most [Bukhari 6464].

options.text: Keep it to himself so nobody thinks less of him
options.feedback: Understandable, but isolation makes slumps deeper. Most Muslims have been there and will get it.

screens.text: **Why it happens.** Newness wears off for everyone; that's how people work. The Qur'an also says believers will be tested, not just left to say "we believe" [Q 29:2].

screens.before: Allah says that when His servant comes toward Him walking, He comes

options.feedback: Yes. On a low day, a small step toward Him is met by far more.
Not quite. He comes running. Your small step on a low day is met by far more.
Not quite. A walking step is enough; He comes running toward it.

screens.title: Lean on people
screens.intro: This is the moment your circle matters most. Converts with Muslim friends and a link to their masjid tend to grow stronger over time [Yaqeen 2025].

steps.text: Pray one prayer a week at {{masjid.name}}

screens.done_text: A slump shared with a friend is half as heavy.

screens.prompt: Look back at what you wrote on Day 1 about why you said yes, and your Day 12 note. Now write a short note to yourself for your next low day. What do you want to remember?

screens.title: Finishing the tashahhud
screens.intro: Today's prayer phrase ends the tashahhud with the shahada: the same words that made you Muslim.

moves.text: Sitting, say the parts of the tashahhud you've learned so far.
Finish with the shahada. Many Muslims raise the right index finger while saying it. {{masjid.name}} will show you its way.
From now on, say the whole tashahhud in every sitting, instead of the shahada alone.
Sitting, say the parts of the tashahhud you've learned so far.
As you say "*la ilaha*" (no god), make a ring with your right thumb and middle finger and raise your index finger.
Lower it at "*illa Allah*" (except Allah), and finish the shahada.

You said yes once. On a flat day, you get to say it again, quietly, in the sitting of every prayer.

prayerPhrase.arabic: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
prayerPhrase.translit: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh
prayerPhrase.meaning: I testify that there is no god except Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger
prayerPhrase.when: Tashahhud part 4, the end of the tashahhud [Bukhari 831]. From now on, say the whole tashahhud in every sitting instead of the shahada alone.

check.prompt: Which is true about feeling low in your faith?

options.text: Feeling low is not leaving Islam; leaving is a choice to reject it
options.feedback: Right. Dips are normal. Keep praying and lean on people while it passes.

options.text: It means you were never really Muslim
options.feedback: Not quite. Even a Companion felt his faith rise and fall, and the Prophet ﷺ reassured him.

check.prompt: You've felt nothing in prayer for a week. What helps most?

options.text: Keep the five prayers, small and steady, and tell a friend or mentor
options.feedback: Right. Regular small deeds and good company carry you through.

options.text: Pause praying until the feeling returns
options.feedback: Not quite. All five stay due, and the feeling usually returns through praying.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The "honeymoon ending" (a few weeks to a few months in) is one of the most common convert experiences: excitement fades, routine sets in, community attention drops, and the question "Did I make the right decision?" can appear [Field Guide ch. 18; Shayan's Reddit research].
- Wording rule: "Feeling low is not leaving Islam. Leaving is a choice to reject it." [SCHOLAR: Q20]
- Hanzalah feared hypocrisy because his faith felt stronger with the Prophet ﷺ than at home (Abu Bakr felt the same); the Prophet ﷺ said there is a time for this and a time for that [Muslim 2750].
- Believers are tested [Q 29:2]; Allah meets a servant's small step with far more [Bukhari 7405]; the deeds Allah loves most are regular ones, even if small [Bukhari 6464].
- Religious Muslim friends and mosque attachment were the strongest predictors of positive faith development for converts [Yaqeen 2025].
- All five prayers remain due during a slump. Never suggest a break or a reduced number.
- Tashahhud finger (Hanafi): ring with the thumb and middle finger, raise the index finger at "la ilaha", lower it at "illa Allah"; no continuous movement [First Instructions on Worship; Darul Ifta Birmingham 20074].

**Likely questions**
- *"I feel nothing when I pray."* Normal; the prayer counts. Suggest slowing down on one phrase they now understand (e.g. the tashahhud's meaning), and praying one prayer with others.
- *"Did I make the right choice?"* Take it seriously, don't argue. Ask what's behind it (loneliness, a rule, people's behavior, a real doubt). Offer the mentor, and if it's a belief question, look at it together gently (Day 33 covers doubts). Never shame.
- *"How do I tell someone I'm struggling?"* Offer a one-line message they can send. Remind them most Muslims have been there.
- *"Three small things for a low day."* The five prayers (even short and simple), one short du'a in their own words, one message to a Muslim friend.

**Escalate:** a convert who says they want to leave Islam (stay warm, no pressure, no threats; offer the mentor or imam); signs of depression, hopelessness or self-harm (safety rule first: 988 and the alert flow).

**Don't**
- Don't use Hell, guilt or fear to push them through a slump.
- Don't say "you're just being tested" as a brush-off; listen first.
- Don't suggest pausing prayer or "doing what you feel like."
- Don't bring up the punishment for apostasy (fixed-policy topic).
madhabNote: **The finger in the tashahhud:** Shafi'is raise the index finger at "illa Allah" and keep it raised; many Malikis move it side to side through the tashahhud; Hanbalis point it each time Allah is mentioned. All are valid practice. Some Hanafi authorities keep it raised to the end.
